changeNote: Owner-authorised focused migration to bank 2.0.0 and axes 2.0.0. Independently reassessed democracy-autocracy-02, democracy-autocracy-04, democracy-autocracy-06, democracy-autocracy-08, democracy-autocracy-11, democracy-autocracy-13 using retained period-specific sourced research and the explicitly recorded supplemental references. All other 234 question-level answer objects are preserved verbatim from revision 1. No other axis was reassessed, no target score or population remapping was applied, and earlier archives remain unchanged. Six new educated assumptions are provisional; retained evidence limitations still apply.

axes.brief:
April2026 competitive election produced a May9 change of prime minister; emergency decree rule ended and July constitutional changes altered judicial and office rules.
Focused six-question reassessment: The retained 2026 dossier records a parliamentary change of government and ending decree rule. Citizen referendum avenues remain subject to exclusions; electoral mandates and emergency continuity create a mixed assessment of the newly bounded postponement claim.
axes.counterEvidence:
Earlier uneven campaigning and captured institutions are relevant inherited constraints, not evidence Orbán remains prime minister. Supermajority reform and stated independence do not prove every court now practically independent.
The owner-defined broader axis includes lawful delegation and direct public control; a lower numerical placement is not a regime classification. Six exact responses and response strengths remain inferred. Retained source access dates are not refreshed unless a source was actually revisited. Unchanged answers and other axes were not re-audited. The retained 2026 dossier records a parliamentary change of government and ending decree rule. Citizen referendum avenues remain subject to exclusions; electoral mandates and emergency continuity create a mixed assessment of the newly bounded postponement claim.

answers.rationale: April12 competitive election replaced the governing majority and May9 parliamentary election installed a new prime minister; national elections recur constitutionally.

Educated assumption: Agree is the most likely response to the revised claim “Important national policy decisions should be delegated to independent experts who do not need approval from elected representatives for each decision.” in the specified scope (Contemporary institutions and implemented policy; intended cut-off 2026-10-04). The retained sourced research records: April2026 competitive election produced a May9 change of prime minister; emergency decree rule ended and July constitutional changes altered judicial and office rules. Focused interpretation: The retained 2026 dossier records a parliamentary change of government and ending decree rule. Citizen referendum avenues remain subject to exclusions; electoral mandates and emergency continuity create a mixed assessment of the newly bounded postponement claim. This is delegation of policy decisions to independent specialists, not replacement of the electorate or a claim that all expertise is political sovereignty. A legislative mandate, appointment process and later review can coexist with not voting on every operational decision. The ECB and national central bank decision bodies must not take instructions from governments or other bodies. Monetary delegation is one important field, not evidence that all national policy is insulated. The described institutional delegation or bounded permission makes agreement more likely than disagreement. Legal safeguards, narrower implementation or an inferred historical application make ordinary agreement more appropriate than an unconditional strong response. The citations supply contextual evidence, not a documented exact response to this new wording. The original source dossier is used as retained research; this pass does not claim a fresh retrieval or complete verification of every historical citation. Precise policy scope, hypothetical institutional translations and response intensity remain uncertain.
Adult suffrage is not education/intelligence-qualified; judicial disqualification and capacity exceptions qualify universality.

Educated assumption: Agree is the most likely response to the revised claim “During a serious emergency, the head of government should be able to put temporary laws into effect before parliament votes, with those laws expiring if parliament rejects them.” in the specified scope (Contemporary institutions and implemented policy; intended cut-off 2026-10-04). The retained sourced research records: April2026 competitive election produced a May9 change of prime minister; emergency decree rule ended and July constitutional changes altered judicial and office rules. Focused interpretation: The retained 2026 dossier records a parliamentary change of government and ending decree rule. Citizen referendum avenues remain subject to exclusions; electoral mandates and emergency continuity create a mixed assessment of the newly bounded postponement claim. This permits temporary lawmaking before a vote but expressly retains parliamentary rejection and expiry. It is not the previous permission to override an actual parliamentary rejection; primary legislation and delegated emergency instruments can differ.  The described institutional delegation or bounded permission makes agreement more likely than disagreement. Legal safeguards, narrower implementation or an inferred historical application make ordinary agreement more appropriate than an unconditional strong response. The citations supply contextual evidence, not a documented exact response to this new wording. The original source dossier is used as retained research; this pass does not claim a fresh retrieval or complete verification of every historical citation. Precise policy scope, hypothetical institutional translations and response intensity remain uncertain.

Educated assumption: Opposition parties can contest and the2026 transfer demonstrates real competition, but inherited media/resource inequalities qualify equal conditions. Post-transition equality across all campaign resources has not been fully measured.

Educated assumption: Agree is the most likely response to the revised claim “Citizens should be able to put proposed national laws to a binding public vote by collecting enough signatures.” in the specified scope (Contemporary institutions and implemented policy; intended cut-off 2026-10-04). The retained sourced research records: April2026 competitive election produced a May9 change of prime minister; emergency decree rule ended and July constitutional changes altered judicial and office rules. Focused interpretation: The retained 2026 dossier records a parliamentary change of government and ending decree rule. Citizen referendum avenues remain subject to exclusions; electoral mandates and emergency continuity create a mixed assessment of the newly bounded postponement claim. The revised claim gives citizens an independent signature-triggered route to a binding national law vote. A petition, advisory consultation, parliamentary bill proposal or government-called referendum does not by itself establish that mechanism. Constitutional initiatives can provide qualified, narrower support.  The described institutional delegation or bounded permission makes agreement more likely than disagreement. Legal safeguards, narrower implementation or an inferred historical application make ordinary agreement more appropriate than an unconditional strong response. The citations supply contextual evidence, not a documented exact response to this new wording. The original source dossier is used as retained research; this pass does not claim a fresh retrieval or complete verification of every historical citation. Precise policy scope, hypothetical institutional translations and response intensity remain uncertain.

Educated assumption: Constitutional review can invalidate unlawful governmental action and July reforms change appointments/terms. Earlier political dependence prevents assuming fully independent implementation immediately; moderate agreement weighs enforceable machinery and inherited constraints.

Educated assumption: Strongly agree is the most likely response to the revised claim “The governing party or coalition should be able to choose a new head of government between elections without holding a new public vote.” in the specified scope (Contemporary institutions and implemented policy; intended cut-off 2026-10-04). The retained sourced research records: April2026 competitive election produced a May9 change of prime minister; emergency decree rule ended and July constitutional changes altered judicial and office rules. Focused interpretation: The retained 2026 dossier records a parliamentary change of government and ending decree rule. Citizen referendum avenues remain subject to exclusions; electoral mandates and emergency continuity create a mixed assessment of the newly bounded postponement claim. This concerns replacing the head of government between elections. Parliamentary confidence or governing-party selection differs from choosing an entirely new legislature. A personally elected presidency has different succession rules, and a prime minister must not be confused with a separate ceremonial or executive head of state.  The contextual institutional mechanism or explicit participatory commitment is sufficiently central to favour a strong response to the defined claim. This is an estimate of response strength, not a claim the subject answered this questionnaire. The citations supply contextual evidence, not a documented exact response to this new wording. The original source dossier is used as retained research; this pass does not claim a fresh retrieval or complete verification of every historical citation. Precise policy scope, hypothetical institutional translations and response intensity remain uncertain.

Educated assumption: Party competition and lawful electoral framework make discretionary ideological exclusion by governing leadership unlikely. Exact current party-dissolution safeguards were not exhaustively traced; unlawful parties are not unrestricted political-position bans.

Article8 permits binding national referendums initiated by200000 voters on parliamentary matters, with turnout and constitutional/budget/treaty exclusions. Repeal can be sought within this qualified scope.

Educated assumption: Agree is the most likely response to the revised claim “An elected head of government should be able to make major policy decisions within existing law without obtaining parliament’s approval for each decision.” in the specified scope (Contemporary institutions and implemented policy; intended cut-off 2026-10-04). The retained sourced research records: April2026 competitive election produced a May9 change of prime minister; emergency decree rule ended and July constitutional changes altered judicial and office rules. Focused interpretation: The retained 2026 dossier records a parliamentary change of government and ending decree rule. Citizen referendum avenues remain subject to exclusions; electoral mandates and emergency continuity create a mixed assessment of the newly bounded postponement claim. The revised claim permits executive policy implementation within existing law without a separate parliamentary vote on each decision. It does not permit overriding legislation, spending authority, courts, or an explicit parliamentary rejection; collegial executives require additional qualification.  The described institutional delegation or bounded permission makes agreement more likely than disagreement. Legal safeguards, narrower implementation or an inferred historical application make ordinary agreement more appropriate than an unconditional strong response. The citations supply contextual evidence, not a documented exact response to this new wording. The original source dossier is used as retained research; this pass does not claim a fresh retrieval or complete verification of every historical citation. Precise policy scope, hypothetical institutional translations and response intensity remain uncertain.
Article21 provides constructive no-confidence initiated by one-fifth of representatives and adopted by an absolute majority electing a replacement prime minister.

Educated assumption: Neutral is the most likely response to the revised claim “Parliament should be able to postpone a scheduled national election during a serious emergency, for a limited period specified in law.” in the specified scope (Contemporary institutions and implemented policy; intended cut-off 2026-10-04). The retained sourced research records: April2026 competitive election produced a May9 change of prime minister; emergency decree rule ended and July constitutional changes altered judicial and office rules. Focused interpretation: The retained 2026 dossier records a parliamentary change of government and ending decree rule. Citizen referendum avenues remain subject to exclusions; electoral mandates and emergency continuity create a mixed assessment of the newly bounded postponement claim. This concerns a legally limited emergency postponement authorised by Parliament, not a leader cancelling elections for political convenience. Constitutional term limits, emergency exceptions and actual independent parliamentary control must be considered separately.  This is a substantive conditional judgement: the described case for functioning government or collective continuity competes with the described limits on independent discretion or public consent. Neither unqualified permission nor unqualified prohibition best represents that tension. It is not a default for absent evidence. The citations supply contextual evidence, not a documented exact response to this new wording. The original source dossier is used as retained research; this pass does not claim a fresh retrieval or complete verification of every historical citation. Precise policy scope, hypothetical institutional translations and response intensity remain uncertain.

Educated assumption: Representative fixed terms and constitutional local dissolution mechanisms do not establish a voter-initiated individual recall. Moderate disagreement is likeliest; every separate current recall statute was not exhaustively searched.
Electoral replacement and parliamentary confidence demonstrate accountability to elected representatives and voters.
Civilian constitutional command does not authorize military replacement of government on the forces’ own judgment.

axes.brief: Civil expression and due-process rights coexist with drug restrictions, police powers and inherited surveillance structures.
axes.counterEvidence: Current political transition and EU court judgments change context; SIM registration does not establish government identification for every online service. Specific searches and multiyear retention require qualified estimates.

answers.rationale: Educated assumption: Drug prohibition and paternalistic controls make unrestricted harmful self-regarding drug use unlikely. Exact current possession/diversion amendments were not fully audited.

Educated assumption: Constitutional privacy alongside criminal investigation powers supports judicially authorized serious-crime interception. Inherited nonjudicial national-security surveillance does not negate this narrower permissible court case; precise updated procedure remains qualified.

Educated assumption: Assembly is protected and current policy favors peaceful public demonstration, with public-order/access limits. Exact temporary-road-obstruction doctrine after May remains unverified.

Educated assumption: Protected political criticism and actual opposition debate support offence-tolerant speech; inherited national-symbol/community-dignity restrictions qualify breadth. Every offence-based case after transition was not audited.

Educated assumption: Health obligations and regulatory public-health powers suggest some compulsory personal-protection measures. Exact authority primarily benefiting the individual, rather than others, is not fully traced.

Educated assumption: Police surveillance capacity coexists with constitutional/data-protection safeguards. Mixed estimate weighs actual collection and purpose limits; years-long suspicion-free movement retention was not verified, so no fabricated storage period is claimed.
Educated assumption: National traffic enforcement and intoxication control make random testing plausible. Exact suspicion-free statutory wording was not retrieved.

Educated assumption: Judicial criminal-prevention and restraint mechanisms make serious-risk movement restriction likely. Exact prospective-harm threshold and updated procedural scope remain uncertain.

Educated assumption: Adults retain broad lawful media access despite restrictions on minors and prohibited content. CJEU judgment and September proposal do not alone establish all domestic repeal, and exact adult restrictions remain qualified.

Educated assumption: Ordinary online platforms remain available without universal government identity verification. Telecom SIM identification is narrower; exact exceptions for all service types were not audited.
Educated assumption: Area security powers and serious-threat prevention suggest suspicion-free searches can occur. Exact credible-violence authorization threshold was not retrieved.

Educated assumption: Assembly law allows prevention of serious disorder subject to rights and review. Exact current threshold is inferred rather than a claim every dissident gathering can be prohibited.

Educated assumption: Constitutional home/privacy protection coexists with prosecutorial/investigative search powers. Mixed answer distinguishes required lawful authorization from an exclusively judicial warrant; full current criminal-procedure exception inventory was not traced.

Educated assumption: Public-finance transparency, reporting safeguards and current anti-corruption direction support disclosure of misconduct, qualified by secrecy offences. Exact publication immunity for confidential documents remains unverified.

Educated assumption: Restrictive civilian weapon licensing makes ordinary defence ownership subject only to violence-history checks unlikely. Special licenses are counterevidence, and their current purpose thresholds were not fully audited.

Educated assumption: Constitutional detention review and EU rights constraints make indefinite terrorism detention at the authorities’ sole discretion unlikely. Inherited due-process deficiencies qualify implementation; exact emergency exceptions remain unverified.

axes.brief: Constitutional Hungarian language, Christian culture and national cohesion coexist with constitutionally recognized nationalities and minority education.
axes.counterEvidence: Actual preschool curriculum preserves minority and refugee-child cultural identity. National civic integration is not legal prohibition of all foreign cultural identity or Indigenous territorial sovereignty.

answers.rationale: Educated assumption: Hungarian language and Christian cultural foundation favor common national priority in conflict. Recognized nationalities and refugee-child identity temper this; no blanket migrant-conflict hierarchy was located.

Educated assumption: Minority-language institutions and preschool identity accommodation indicate funded cultural accommodation. Exact spending obligations for every migrant practice were not verified.

Educated assumption: Common civic participation and national culture suggest some customs integration, qualified by explicit preservation of distinct identity. No total cultural-conversion duty is asserted.
Constitutional nationalities are constituent parts of the political community, and preschool rules preserve refugee-child identity alongside integration.
Hungarian is constitutionally the official language and primary language of national administration, with minority-language exceptions.

Educated assumption: Nationalities are constitutionally acknowledged, but they are not automatically an officially designated Indigenous category. Mixed estimate weighs recognition and uncertain Indigenous ceremonial applicability rather than inventing a specific ceremony duty.

Educated assumption: National heritage and Christian/Hungarian cultural commitments suggest predominant-tradition funding priority; minority institutions are counterevidence. Current allocation shares were not measured.

Educated assumption: Shared constitutional community and national culture suggest common priority, qualified by protected nationality identity. Exact cultural-conflict adjudication hierarchy remains uncertain.
Educated assumption: National institutional calendars and Christian holidays make a broadly common schedule likely. Every minority-celebration accommodation was not audited.
Recognized nationalities, their languages/cultures and self-government are constitutionally part of the national political community.
Educated assumption: Preschool rules explicitly connect preserved refugee identity with social integration, making wider participation likely. Adult migrant programme coverage remains unverified.

Educated assumption: Official Hungarian and local nationality language protection support mixed signage. Migrant foreign-language signage entitlement is not equivalent to historical minority-language rights and was not fully traced.

Educated assumption: Family education and national patriotic values coexist with minority identity transmission. Mixed response reflects explicit dual strands, not an assumption all families must rank one first.

Educated assumption: Religious freedom and face-identification/security rules may coexist. The precise exception preserving burqa when every other full covering is prohibited was not found; competing liberty and security constraints support a qualified interaction estimate.
Constitutional nationality recognition and minority/refugee-child cultural preservation include distinct ways of life, qualified by predominant Christian/Hungarian framework.

Educated assumption: National cohesion and common civic integration suggest some shared-custom emphasis; explicit distinct-identity preschool protection is counterevidence. Adult programmes’ precise customs-versus-maintenance emphasis remains unverified.

axes.brief: Restricted temporary-worker admission and category exclusions coexist with EU mobility, skilled permits, family reunification and protection categories.
axes.counterEvidence: 35000 temporary-work quota is not an all-permanent or family quota. No eligible guest-worker nationality does not mean no employment-purpose permit, Blue Card or recognized asylum.

answers.rationale: Educated assumption: The35000 quota regulates temporary employment, not a universal permanent housing/workforce ceiling. Moderate disagreement fits this exact permanent numerical limit; the complete current permanent admission inventory was not traced.
Permit categories and conditions do not provide a general economic-improvement settlement entitlement for all foreigners; EU mobility is a substantial exception.
Family, protected and long-term status categories coexist with skilled employment; useful skills are not the only permanent criterion.
Permanent/long-term residents can sponsor qualifying partners/dependent children, subject to category and financial conditions; temporary guest-worker exclusion is not permanent-family exclusion.

Educated assumption: Recognized protection exists, but restrictive asylum access and status scrutiny make unconditional permanent settlement regardless of compatibility unlikely. Exact current permanent entitlement after recognition remains qualified.

Official employer guidance provides expulsion when a third-country national no longer has a right to stay after permit refusal/revocation. Protection and nonrefoulement exceptions qualify disagreement; this is not blanket removal of every asylum claimant.
Guest-worker status is temporary and barred from the national residency card; employer demand does not independently permit permanent settlement.

Educated assumption: Current restricted work categories and national-employment priority suggest restraint despite economic demand. Exact housing/public-service tradeoff remains inferred, rather than a documented quota rationale for every entrant.

Educated assumption: Temporary employment quota is not a common permanent-family quota. Moderate disagreement is likeliest; family permit conditions are documented but universal cap arithmetic was not found.
Employer-backed permit pathways coexist with nationality/category restrictions and Blue Card requirements. A job offer alone is insufficient; EU mobility and approved permits provide real access.

Educated assumption: Employer/family evidence matters in many routes, while independent long-term residence and protection complicate a universal sponsor requirement. Mixed estimate reflects distinct categories; every current permanent pathway was not fully traced.

Educated assumption: Study completion alone is not a permanent-residence entitlement; work/other qualifying status is generally needed. Exact current post-study transition routes were not exhaustively audited.

Educated assumption: Protection exceptions and nonrefoulement coexist with restrictive entry/access practices. Mixed response weighs legal protection outside work quotas and actual entry limits; current cap-reached scenarios are unverified.

Educated assumption: Nationality-limited work admission and regional ties suggest some culturally proximate preference, qualified by nonregional skilled/family/EU routes. Nationality eligibility is not itself proof of a wholly cultural ranking.
Recognized immigrant/resident/refugee family categories receive child-protection coverage; benefit/social-housing conditions differ, so agreement is qualified rather than universal.

Educated assumption: Current category selection and national-cohesion approach do not establish increased admission specifically for cultural difference. Moderate disagreement is likeliest; diversity within lawful routes is counterevidence, not a diversity-volume objective.

axes.brief: Voluntary armed forces and reserves, NATO commitments and defence modernization support deterrence and collective defence.
axes.counterEvidence: Current policy avoids deployment into Russia–Ukraine war.2035 spending commitment is future; KFOR participation does not demonstrate prolonged offensive war capability or no military obligations at all.

answers.rationale: Educated assumption: NATO/KFOR overseas missions coexist with present avoidance of Russia–Ukraine deployment. Mixed estimate distinguishes nondefensive security participation from unilateral war for national gain; comprehensive current force-use doctrine was not retrieved.

Educated assumption: Current war-avoidance and alliance diplomacy suggest negotiation priority, qualified by maintained collective-defence force. Exact willingness to accept slower outcomes remains inferred.

Educated assumption: Modernization and future NATO spending commitment support substantial deterrence expenditure, but not independently superior forces against every potential opponent. Moderate agreement is qualified;2035 target is not current spending achieved.
Educated assumption: Collective defence and readiness make action against a strongly evidenced imminent attack plausible. Specific preemption doctrine was not located, so agreement is moderate.

Educated assumption: Collective defence predominates while KFOR and other security missions need not follow an attack against Hungary/allies. Mixed estimate addresses that literal only condition rather than equating all overseas service with aggression.
Current ordinary recruitment and reserve service are voluntary; constitution permits male wartime obligations, qualifying disagreement with routine mandatory service.

Educated assumption: Avoidance of participation in Russia–Ukraine war suggests meaningful diplomatic compromise, qualified by NATO obligations. Exact substantial-concession threshold remains unverified.

Educated assumption: EU/alliance safety/accountability context makes unrestricted autonomous lethal targeting unlikely. AI strategy does not specify weapons, and no current national human-approval doctrine was found.
Educated assumption: Territorial/collective defence and reserves dominate, qualified by KFOR deployment. Precise force-planning allocation between defence and expeditionary action was not measured.
NATO collective-defence commitments and maintained armed forces reject avoiding all action even when an ally is attacked.

Educated assumption: Overseas KFOR capability and national modernization coexist with limited verified prolonged high-intensity expeditionary capability. Mixed estimate distinguishes deployed peace support from sustained foreign combat; actual combat endurance was not established.
Educated assumption: Current diplomatic security policy makes avoiding war over unresolved territory likelier. No exact national territorial-dispute rule was found.

Educated assumption: Current alliance diplomacy and no Ukraine combat deployment make unilateral coercive military threats unlikely. Collective deterrence is counterevidence; precise dispute-threat doctrine remains uncertain.
Educated assumption: War-risk reduction and restrained deployment suggest de-escalation priority, qualified by collective deterrence. Exact resolve-versus-risk hierarchy was not documented.
Educated assumption: National defence/intelligence structures make military intelligence collection likely despite diplomatic risks. Specific foreign espionage policy is not publicly established.

Educated assumption: Alliance deterrence modernization coexists with multilateral arms-control commitments. Mixed estimate weighs reciprocal negotiated reductions and capability priorities; current willingness to accept particular reductions was not located.

axes.brief: EU, NATO and retained ICC membership pool binding legal and security powers while national currency and constitutional identity retain autonomy.
axes.counterEvidence: May29 reversal prevented ICC withdrawal taking effect. Earlier noncompliance remains inherited implementation evidence, not proof of absence of international legal obligations or current withdrawal.

answers.rationale: Constitutional national identity/sovereignty coexist with ArticleE joint EU powers and binding obligations; neither entirely exclusive national nor unrestricted international authority applies.
EU treaty obligations and judgments bind Hungary even against government objections; compliance deficits qualify practical breadth.
EU/ICC membership and binding European judgment limit exclusive national-court finality; constitutional sovereignty reservations and inherited defiance qualify disagreement.
EU and NATO membership create long-term obligations and shared decisions, including national freedom-of-action limits.
Treaty withdrawal mechanisms preserve national choice subject to notice/procedure, not a general international veto; reversed ICC withdrawal confirms national notification choice.
Hungary retained Rome Statute membership after May29 reversal and remains subject to European judicial obligations. Enforcement/compliance limitations qualify strength.

Educated assumption: National constitutional identity and own interests coexist with new government’s explicit renewed EU/NATO cooperation. Mixed estimate reflects both implemented treaty pooling and sovereign reservations; every current conflict outcome is not observed.

Educated assumption: EU environmental rules and cross-border cooperation share binding powers. Exact acceptance of further institutional environmental authority remains uncertain, so agreement is moderate.
Hungary remains in the EU, whose common foreign/security policy entails shared commitments and decisions despite veto areas.
Binding European rights/legal obligations can require legal change, including April CJEU judgment. Actual implementation is incomplete rather than proof no binding authority exists.
Hungary retains the forint and its national central bank rather than current shared euro monetary policy.
EU budget and shared policy programmes pool funding and decision-making on common problems.
EU/Schengen and asylum obligations share border authority, qualified by national enforcement and inherited restrictive practice.
EU customs/single-market membership implements common negotiated trade rules rather than wholly independent Hungarian schedules.

Educated assumption: Current membership pools specific competences but is not accession to a sovereign international political federation. Moderate agreement preserves that distinction; future federation intentions are unverified.

Educated assumption: Current NATO/EU cooperation and retained ICC status support collective enforcement, qualified by national discretion and no Ukraine troop deployment. Specific neutrality-versus-interest cases remain uncertain.

axes.brief: Private enterprise coexists with state MVM utilities, MÁV infrastructure, development banking, hospitals and public broadcasting.
axes.counterEvidence: Privatized rail maintenance does not mean infrastructure privatized; state contract auditing does not nationalize4iG. Predominant owner occupation does not imply a large public rental stock.

answers.rationale: Private companies dominate most economic sectors despite substantial state and connected-owner involvement.
MVM is wholly state-owned and owns substantial energy networks; ownership is distinct from price regulation.

Educated assumption: Private economic predominance coexists with retained strategic public companies and state acquisitions. Mixed response weighs actual comparable-provider choice without inventing a universal cost-quality ownership test.
State-owned MVM operates commercially across energy and supplementary industries, while private competition remains; state businesses are not confined solely to monopolies.
Public hospitals and national healthcare institutions remain alongside private facilities; out-of-pocket financing is not proof of private ownership of all facilities.
MÁV infrastructure remains state railway property; vehicle-maintenance privatization is a separate transaction.

Educated assumption: Actual private rail maintenance and contracted provision make comparable-cost outsourcing plausible. Every public-service procurement quality/access decision was not audited, so agreement is moderate.
MFB is exclusively state-owned and explicitly works alongside commercial/private banking institutions.

Educated assumption: State strategic ownership remains and new4iG contract audits are not a programme of wholesale commercial privatization. Selective past maintenance sales are counterevidence; current sale plans were not comprehensively traced.

Educated assumption: Owner-occupied housing predominates and a substantial nationwide public rental share was not established. Local municipal housing exists; current exact stock share was not retrieved.

Educated assumption: Mixed state/private strategic ownership and regulated private operations coexist. Mixed estimate reflects actual security review without assuming regulation always suffices or every strategic business must be state-owned.

Educated assumption: Public energy assets and mineral/resource controls coexist with private extraction and concessions. Ownership of underground resources does not establish public ownership of extracting companies; current all-sector shares remain unmeasured.

Educated assumption: Actual concession/contract provision and private rail maintenance suggest ordinary routine-service contracting where practical. Moderate agreement is likeliest, qualified by retained public providers and unverified current ownership of every waste operator. A mixed national energy holding or contract audit alone is not proof of routine municipal delivery.

Educated assumption: MVM/MÁV strategic ownership remains despite potential sale proceeds; selective sales are counterevidence. Exact explicit revenue-versus-retention decisions after transition were not audited.

Educated assumption: Public enterprise support coexists with restructuring and selective private maintenance ownership. Mixed estimate distinguishes repeated financial support from a documented mandatory privatization rule, which was not located.
National public broadcasting ownership persists alongside private media; political capture is a separate governance issue, not private legal ownership.

axes.brief: EU customs/single-market rules facilitate trade while sectoral controls, agricultural protection and foreign-investment screening constrain uniform openness.
axes.counterEvidence: Distortive policies identified June2026 are implementation evidence, not all future reforms. Common external tariffs and shared trade authority differ from unilateral Hungarian import setting.

answers.rationale: Educated assumption: EU common external tariffs/protection coexist with tariff-free intra-EU trade. Moderate agreement addresses domestic-industry protection, though every Hungary-specific current tariff preference was not documented.
Single-market integration removes most internal trade barriers, qualified by actual sectoral distortions and external trade protection.

Educated assumption: EU procurement nondiscrimination coexists with documented national-champion favoritism. Mixed estimate distinguishes implemented supplier preference from a universal rule to pay more for domestic supply; exact current cases remain incomplete.

Educated assumption: Open supply chains and EU trade coexist with sanctions/strategic restrictions. Moderate agreement fits ordinary commercial purchasing; all-country unrestricted permission is not asserted.

Educated assumption: Open essential supply chains coexist with sectoral security/production protection. Mixed estimate reflects real import access and national-capacity priorities; a general essential-goods import ban was not found.

Educated assumption: EU collective trade commitments coexist with reciprocal negotiations and protection. Mixed estimate distinguishes internal unilateral openness from external reciprocal policy; exact unconditional Hungarian liberalization preference is not documented.

Educated assumption: Subsidized national champions coexist with EU market/access constraints. Mixed estimate distinguishes subsidies from literal temporary import restrictions for infant industries, whose exact current scope was not verified.
Foreign investment is important but strategic screening and actual unequal treatment prevent uniform parity; ordinary establishment remains open in many sectors.

Educated assumption: Agricultural protective policy and EU external barriers favor preserving domestic capacity, qualified by intra-EU trade. Exact October2026 Hungary-specific import restrictions were not fully traced.

Educated assumption: Competitive export/private industries coexist with protected selected sectors and distortive subsidies. Mixed response reflects implemented sector variation rather than an uncertainty default.
Educated assumption: EU trade-defense and retaliatory authority make calibrated reciprocal tariff responses likely. Exact current Hungarian support for every retaliation case was not retrieved.

Educated assumption: EU product-tax nondiscrimination generally applies, while sectoral taxes can burden foreign-owned retailers disproportionately. Ownership effects are not identical to legally different taxes on imported products; specific product exceptions were not exhaustively audited.

Educated assumption: EU anti-subsidy framework supports proportionate import protection against subsidized foreign firms. Exact Hungary-specific implementation preferences were not separately located.
EU negotiated tariff reductions and single-market supply chains accept foreign-supplier dependence, qualified by strategic safeguards.
Strategic foreign-investment screening and state intervention constrain foreign control; no complete blanket foreign-ownership ban is claimed.

Educated assumption: EU cross-border digital-service access supports ordinary foreign online purchases. Restricted unlawful content/sanctions are exceptions; no complete Hungary-specific foreign-service barrier inventory was audited.

axes.brief: Market production, employer wages and enterprise decisions coexist with subsidies, development-bank direction and retained retail/utility controls in ordinary parliamentary law.
axes.counterEvidence: Ending emergency decree governance did not itself repeal all economic controls. No universal central output plan or government-directed independent central-bank rate policy is assumed.

answers.rationale: Private firms ordinarily choose production, qualified by sectoral controls and state-directed financing.

Educated assumption: National subsidies and industrial priorities do not establish broad compulsory production targets. Moderate disagreement distinguishes incentives and regulated public utilities from literal mandatory output quotas; exact current sector exceptions remain unverified.
Market prices generally apply, qualified by retained retail-margin and utility controls in ordinary law.
Development-bank financing and sectoral investment subsidies direct resources to selected economic priorities, without a universal mandatory production plan.
Private firms generally expand/close according to demand, qualified by subsidies retaining less productive firms and regulatory constraints.
May ordinary statute retained essential retail margin limits and energy price compensation; ending emergency decree rule did not abolish these controls.

Educated assumption: Private market entry generally does not require showing national need for output, but concessions/strict services regulation restrict entry. Precise current need-test exceptions were not exhaustively audited.
MFB explicitly channels favorable finance into development priorities and gaps, alongside private banks; not all bank lending is compulsory.

Educated assumption: EU capital mobility and internationally integrated enterprise favor ordinary outward transfers without general approval, qualified by sanctions/reporting. Exact current category exceptions were not fully retrieved.
Actual sectoral subsidy schemes steer investment and retain companies; Commission recommendations to reduce distortions do not mean already abolished.

Educated assumption: Regulated crypto/private payment instruments coexist with national forint legal-money authority. Mixed response distinguishes owning digital assets from rival fully recognized currencies; precise current issuance restrictions were not traced.
A national statutory minimum wage applies; generally negotiated higher wages do not remove the floor.
Ordinary private wages are negotiated, qualified by minimum wage and public-sector scales.

Educated assumption: Constitutional central-bank autonomy and own monetary institutions make direct government plan-control unlikely. State credit support is separate; actual current informal influence remains uncertain.
Educated assumption: Private rent and owner-occupied market housing dominate, with municipal/subsidized exceptions. Exact current rent-control scope was not comprehensively traced.

Educated assumption: Ordinary private production predominates over comprehensive national coordination, despite substantial selected-sector intervention. No current economy-wide mandatory distribution system was established.

axes.brief: Cash pensions/family support and new targeted school-start assistance coexist with flat income tax, phased mother exemptions and limited working-age support.
axes.counterEvidence: Tax relief and subsidized services are not cash income. Proposals for new rates are not enacted; inheritance exemptions and exact earmarking distinguish a transmission duty from large-estate cash redistribution.

answers.rationale: Educated assumption: Pensions/family cash support and targeted new assistance coexist with flat income taxation and weak working-age support. Mixed estimate reflects actual distributional mechanisms without attributing all earlier Orbán preferences to the new government.

Educated assumption: Flat personal income tax and family exemptions favor limiting progressive extraction, qualified by cash support and public pensions. The new government’s precise inequality-alone tax principle is not fully observed.

Educated assumption: New targeted school-start cash support coexists with retained low-tax structure and modest minimum-income protection. Mixed answer distinguishes implemented additional benefit from an adopted tax-financed stronger general income floor.

Educated assumption: Limited working-age support and targeted eligibility favor a safety-net function, qualified by broad family/pension benefits. Current distributional narrowing magnitude was not measured.

Current consolidated Income Tax ActSection8 sets ordinary personal income tax at15percent. It does not impose substantially larger tax shares solely because ordinary earnings are higher; specific mother/age/family exemptions qualify the comparison without an invented enacted progressive scale.

Educated assumption: Mother exemptions and tax relief let households retain earnings, while redistributive cash programmes remain. Exact post-May willingness to accept larger differences is inferred rather than quoted.

Educated assumption: Inheritance duties coexist with broad close-family exemptions; a specific large-estate revenue earmark for low-resource cash support was not established. Mixed answer reflects actual duty and narrow family scope, not claiming no transmission tax.

Educated assumption: Historically90-day unemployment support and workfare retain time-limit context; no enacted general indefinite extension was verified. Exact post-May current duration for every working-age benefit remains qualified.

Educated assumption: No implemented broad recurring accumulated-wealth tax funding low-income transfers was established. Local property duties exist; every current wealth-tax exception was not exhaustively traced.

Educated assumption: Modest working-age assistance and tax exemptions suggest restrained funding burdens, qualified by new targeted cash spending. Current government’s exact fiscal tradeoff is unverified.

Educated assumption: Weak minimum benefits and access difficulties make sufficient ordinary-social-participation income unlikely. Pensions/family benefits vary, and exact October2026 adequacy across all eligible groups was not measured.

Educated assumption: Implemented firewood VAT/mother relief coexist with adopted new vulnerable-family cash assistance. Mixed estimate reflects real changes in both directions rather than pretending one universal budget priority was documented.

Educated assumption: Family-linked tax credits and cash benefits support some low-paid workers, qualified by exclusions for childless/low-tax-liability households. Exact refundable supplement coverage was not fully audited.

Current Income Tax ActSection8 applies the same15percent ordinary marginal personal tax rate regardless of earnings rank, qualified by categorical mother/age/family exemptions. Campaign proposals are not an enacted graduated rate.

Educated assumption: Private property and regulated farmland institutions do not establish a current compensatory large-land redistribution programme. Moderate disagreement is likeliest; a complete2026 land-transfer inventory was not available.
Broad contributory pensions and family-related benefits extend beyond households unable to meet basic needs; targeted new school assistance is one narrower exception.

axes.brief: Christianity is constitutionally recognized and church schools/funding have privileges, alongside civil courts and freedom of religion/nonbelief.
axes.counterEvidence: Christian historical foundation is not clerical final approval, an official faith parliament seat or religious courts controlling civil marriage. Religious/civil consultation on abortion is not clerical veto.

answers.rationale: Christian constitutional foundations coexist with civil legislation and religious freedom; legal enactment is not wholly scripture-based or wholly without religious reference.
Christian constitutional culture and national foundation supply an official normative reference, qualified by civil law and freedom of other faiths.
Religious/civil consultation on abortion is advisory; constitutional civil government does not require clergy approval of policy.
Constitutional national avowal expressly recognizes Christianity’s nation-preserving role and protects Christian culture.

Educated assumption: Secular ethics/nonconfessional options coexist with church instruction and institutions. Mixed estimate reflects actual alternatives, with full current curriculum/opt-out procedures not traced.

Educated assumption: Faith-oriented church education and state support allow cultivated religious belief, qualified by nonconfessional alternatives and no single compulsory state-faith conversion. Exact public-school optional provision remains uncertain.
State courts apply civil statutes, not religious-authority rulings as national law.

Educated assumption: Constitutional civil enactment and advisory consultations make an official clerical law-review mandate unlikely. Exact consultation duties across all legislation were not exhaustively traced.

Educated assumption: Christian civic symbolism and church/state ceremonies coexist with secular public proceedings. Mixed estimate weighs both; current government’s complete ceremonial worship practice was not audited.
Public church-school/institution support and religious designated tax allocation strengthen faith-oriented activities, qualified by wider social-service funding purposes.

Educated assumption: Constitutional Christian identity and national symbols coexist with civil institutional functions. Mixed response distinguishes historical symbols from required endorsement in every government building; current display inventory is unverified.
Christian major-festival holidays remain officially recognized, qualified by secular calendar functions and religious freedom.
Religious office alone provides no automatic parliamentary/government seat under civil constitutional selection.

Educated assumption: Recognized churches receive designated tax allocation and preferential treatment, beyond ordinary civic charities in some respects. Exact2026 religion-specific tax exemption inventory was not retrieved; allocation is not itself every tax exemption.
Civil marriage law requires civil institutional validity, not approval by religious leaders.

Educated assumption: Civil courts/marriage institutions make binding religious family-court decisions unlikely. Private religious observance remains; every recognition/enforcement exception was not exhaustively audited.

axes.brief: Current constitutional male–female marriage and traditional family provisions remain, with legal personal autonomy and some new government openness.
axes.counterEvidence: CJEU judgment and September legislative proposals are assessed separately from enacted national repeal. Legal abortion or registered partnership does not measure public acceptance; maternity support alone does not prove immutable gender behavior.

answers.rationale: Educated assumption: Current government openness and European legal challenge coexist with retained constitutional traditions. Mixed estimate concerns implemented social institutions, not automatic adoption of every new rhetoric.

Educated assumption: Constitutional Christian culture and retained family/sex definitions favor preservation, qualified by current reform proposals and legal personal autonomy. Exact implemented hierarchy for every custom remains uncertain.

Educated assumption: Male–female marriage/family framework and prior adoption restrictions privilege traditional household recognition, while new single-parent/foster cash support recognizes other families. Exact current recognition parity remains unverified.

Educated assumption: Constitutional mother-woman/father-man language and family policy suggest traditional role encouragement. Equal civil opportunity and current change direction qualify this; definitions are not alone proof of compulsory household roles.
Current ArticleL defines marriage between a man and woman; a new prime minister and proposals have not changed that constitutional rule.

Educated assumption: Retained constitutional family framework and family benefits favor traditional married parenting, qualified by support to single-parent/foster households. Exact social-recognition preference under current ministries is inferred.

Educated assumption: Legal early abortion coexists with restrictive counselling/heartbeat regulation and ongoing consultation about repeal. Mixed estimate concerns institutional acceptance; legality does not measure citizen approval and consultation is not completed repeal.

Educated assumption: Constitutional parental education rights and inherited sexual-content restrictions favor parental traditional-values discretion. CJEU judgment limits discriminatory restrictions; exact current opt-out rules were not fully traced.

Educated assumption: Retained marriage/family definitions and inherited adoption restrictions make equal institutional acceptance unlikely, qualified by changed government openness. No public acceptance survey or complete post-May adoption amendments were audited.

Educated assumption: Civil personal autonomy and no general modest-dress mandate make official traditional modesty guidance less likely. Christian historical symbolism is counterevidence, not a documented dress rule; precise current codes remain uncertain.

Educated assumption: Retained constitutional binary-sex language and inherited legal gender restrictions favor conventional official terminology. Current reform proposals qualify but do not establish every enacted identity-language change.
Actual preschool curriculum teaches national/Christian cultural values and established moral/community norms, while respecting individual development and differences.

Educated assumption: Equal legal opportunity and individual autonomy support adults across role choices, qualified by constitutional family roles and persistent institutional discrimination. Exact government recognition practices after May remain unmeasured.

Educated assumption: Rapid political/constitutional reform coexists with retained social provisions and consultation. Mixed estimate distinguishes actual political speed from a universal social-change tempo; no complete popular-demand tradeoff was observed.

Educated assumption: CJEU judgment rejects discriminatory identity-content suppression, while September national amendments remain proposals and inherited school/parent rules persist. Mixed response weighs legal obligation and uncertain fully implemented inclusive teaching, not treating one court ruling as nationwide curriculum delivery.

Educated assumption: Constitutional heritage and national identity protection favor continuity with earlier generations. Current openness provides counterevidence; exact practical-purpose-independent custom hierarchy remains inferred.

axes.brief: AI strategy, energy and infrastructure investment support technology while constitutional GMO-free agriculture and EU safety/environmental law impose caution.
axes.counterEvidence: Strategy goals are not universal AI deployment or acceptance of healthy-person implants, embryo enhancement or cultivated meat. Specific technologies are assessed separately.

answers.rationale: Educated assumption: Adopted AI/industrial modernization coexists with EU safety and constitutional ecological precaution. Mixed estimate reflects technology-specific implementation, not universal early-benefit permission.

Educated assumption: AI strategy and investment allow deployment, while medical/GMO/environmental controls require evidence. A blanket small-trial restriction is not established; technologies have different regimes.

Educated assumption: Actual energy/transport construction and investment promotion suggest substantial benefits can justify some habitat loss under assessment. Exact current irreversible-loss approval decisions were not fully audited.

Educated assumption: EU medical safety authorization supports caution before widespread use, qualified by regulated innovation access. Exact long-term-study threshold for every novel medical technology was not traced.

Educated assumption: Adopted AI productivity strategy and retraining orientation favor use despite occupational change. Adoption goals do not prove every replacing system implemented; exact many-jobs tradeoff remains inferred.

Educated assumption: Constitutional environmental protection coexists with infrastructure/energy expansion. Mixed estimate reflects real development and conservation duties, not assuming either always wins.

Educated assumption: GMO-free agricultural identity and food-safety caution make premature cultivated-meat replacement unlikely. Cultivated meat differs from GMO crops; exact current national approval policy was not found.

Educated assumption: Medical safety framework makes healthy-person brain enhancement research restriction likely until strong evidence. No specific current implant law was retrieved, so this is qualified technological inference.

Educated assumption: Energy-technology and nuclear/renewable investment coexist with efficiency and conservation measures. Mixed estimate distinguishes implemented technologies from unproven large-scale priority, which was not comprehensively documented.

Educated assumption: Environmental assessment duties support delay where major effects remain poorly understood, qualified by national-priority project procedures. Exact post-May implementation consistency was not audited.

Educated assumption: Medical safety/precaution make basic-safety-only healthy-person implants unlikely. AI and biotechnology investment do not authorize invasive enhancement; exact national implant decisions are unavailable.

Educated assumption: Regulated medical devices and safety/equality requirements favor verified supervised diagnosis before wider rollout. Exact different-patient-group reliability threshold was not retrieved.

Educated assumption: Biomedical/EU safety context makes embryo editing for enhancement unlikely. Constitutional GMO-free agriculture is not a human embryo rule; no actual enhancement-trial authorization was located.
Constitutional health provision specifies GMO-free agriculture, imposing stronger restriction than yield benefits alone; it does not ban all medical gene technology.

Educated assumption: Actual rail/housing/energy investment suggests development priority in some land conflicts, qualified by constitutional habitat protection. Comprehensive current project-versus-undeveloped-land choices were not audited.

Educated assumption: Constitutional environmental/public-health protection and strong GMO precaution make delay of potentially irreversible harm likely. No uniform all-technology evidence test was found.

axes.brief: Unitary national law, police, curricula and healthcare coexist with protected local administration, local tax decisions and nationality self-government.
axes.counterEvidence: Constitutional local taxation is not control of most collected national revenue. Court-mediated legality supervision is not an unrestricted executive regional veto, and nationalities are not automatically Indigenous territorial governments.

answers.rationale: Constitutional local self-administration and rulemaking protect a defined sphere, qualified by national law and weak inherited municipal resources.
National statutory competencies and constitutional hierarchy govern disputes, qualified by court review rather than unlimited executive discretion.
Unitary indivisible national territory does not authorize unilateral regional referendum secession.

Educated assumption: National law and legality supervision can displace incompatible local policies, qualified by court procedures and constitutionally defined local competence. Exact programme-only executive override is unverified.
Local organizational rules operate under national constitution/statutes, not independent regional constitutions.
National constitutional police and national government direction govern rather than separate sovereign regional police authority.

Educated assumption: National tax/resource allocation and inherited reduced municipal revenue make keeping most collected taxes unlikely. Local taxation exists; exact2026 overall retained shares were not measured.
A national education framework and compulsory curriculum apply; local delivery does not create separate regional compulsory standards.
Article32 permits local governments to choose local tax types/rates within national law, so location-based differences are legally possible.
National labor legislation sets employment conditions, rather than independent regional dismissal/hour laws.

Educated assumption: Local referendums and organizational discretion coexist with nationally prescribed competencies/boundaries. Moderate disagreement fits changing powers/boundaries without any national approval; exact boundary procedures were not fully audited.
National health institutions and coverage policy determine public treatment entitlement rather than separate regional insurance benefit packages.

Educated assumption: Nationality self-government protects cultural local affairs but is not automatically Indigenous territorial jurisdiction. Mixed response weighs real nationality institutions and uncertain applicability of the literal Indigenous category.
National statutory fiscal limits constrain local tax decisions and borrowing, rather than unlimited regional tax competition.

Educated assumption: Local planning/administration coexist with national environmental duties and protected-resource supervision. Mixed estimate reflects divided scope for genuinely local effects; exact wildlife competence inventory was not retrieved.
National constitutional disaster/security coordination directs multiregion emergencies; local administration does not supply a veto over national response.

axes.brief: Actual preschool curriculum explicitly integrates genetic maturation with environmental influence and teaches cooperation, self-control, attention and moral learning.
axes.counterEvidence: It quantifies no predominant cause for every trait, race, international IQ score or pay-gap. Traditional legal sex categories do not establish a biological predominance theory of gender behavior.

answers.rationale: Educated assumption: Actual curriculum expressly says genetic traits, maturation and environmental influences jointly shape development, while surroundings have a determining role in personal unfolding. Mixed estimate best fits the unquantified predominance claim; it is not uncertainty alone.

Educated assumption: Individualized learning and equal-opportunity intervention make inherited national IQ predominance unlikely. Curriculum measures no international IQ decomposition, so moderate disagreement is an extension rather than documented country ranking.

Educated assumption: Gender-role constitutional language coexists with learned social/educational development and explicit biology–environment interaction. Mixed response distinguishes legal sex definitions from an adopted causal predominance theory of behavior.

Educated assumption: Genetic maturation and emotional-security experiences are explicitly combined. For stress sensitivity specifically, interaction is likeliest; no biological predominance comparison was quantified.

Educated assumption: Curriculum builds on individual curiosity, varied experiences and opportunities, giving learned interests weight. Exact experiences-versus-inherited predominance remains unquantified.

Educated assumption: Life-skills, flexible adaptation and learned problem solving favor experience in risk responses. Curriculum also recognizes biology; no risk-taking-specific hereditary ranking was located.
Educated assumption: Shared activities and learned community habits explicitly develop cooperation. Moderate predominance is likeliest, but curriculum does not quantify inherited contributions.

Educated assumption: Preschool socialization explicitly cultivates empathy and helpfulness. This supports learned contribution rather than inherited predominance; exact comparative empathy causation remains inferred.

Educated assumption: Curriculum explicitly develops attention through environment while tailoring intervention to individual development/needs and maturation. Mixed interaction best fits this trait; no predominant cause was measured.

Educated assumption: Established moral/social reactions are taught through social experience and modeled behavior. Immediate intuitive reactions differ from instructed norms, so biological predominance is only moderately rejected.
Educated assumption: Emotional safety, communication and learned resilience indicate experience shapes perceived threat. Exact threat-perception predominance was not quantified.

Educated assumption: Curriculum recognizes individual genetic/maturational needs and environmental effects together. For temperament specifically, an interaction estimate is likeliest rather than assuming education excludes biology.

Educated assumption: National/multicultural learned values and experience suggest cultural attractiveness preferences. Exact attractiveness causation was not addressed, so agreement is moderate contextual inference.

Educated assumption: Anti-prejudice curriculum and social disadvantage interventions favor contextual rather than racial-biological violence hierarchy. No official adopted racial genetic-violence ranking was found.

Educated assumption: Socialization explicitly teaches self-discipline and persistence through practice/modeling, making learning predominance likely over racial inherited tendencies. No race-specific genetic comparison was measured.

Educated assumption: Equal-opportunity institutions and documented social/workforce barriers give social expectations explanatory weight for pay gaps. Traditional family policy is counterevidence, not a measured finding of lesser inherent economic value; exact decomposition remains uncertain.

review.notes: Reviewed the literal revised mechanisms, directions, period-specific retained research, supplemental references, inferred intensity, conditional Neutral decisions, institutional mismatches and unchanged-answer preservation. New educated-assumption IDs: democracy-autocracy-02, democracy-autocracy-04, democracy-autocracy-06, democracy-autocracy-08, democracy-autocracy-11, democracy-autocracy-13. The retained 2026 dossier records a parliamentary change of government and ending decree rule. Citizen referendum avenues remain subject to exclusions; electoral mandates and emergency continuity create a mixed assessment of the newly bounded postponement claim. All earlier evidence limitations remain. No new empirical calibration, fresh full-profile research, human review or external peer certification is claimed. Similarity is reviewed after scoring the complete batch, without tuning any answer.
